# Fetch any series from the Bank of England Statistical Database

The core data retrieval function. Fetches one or more series by their
BoE series codes and returns a tidy data frame. Use this when the
convenience functions (e.g.
[`boe_bank_rate()`](https://charlescoverdale.github.io/boe/reference/boe_bank_rate.md),
[`boe_exchange_rate()`](https://charlescoverdale.github.io/boe/reference/boe_exchange_rate.md))
do not cover the series you need.

## Usage

``` r
boe_get(series_codes, from = "1960-01-01", to = Sys.Date(), cache = TRUE)
```

## Source

<https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/boeapps/database/>

## Arguments

- series_codes:

  Character vector of one or more BoE series codes.

- from:

  Date or character (YYYY-MM-DD). Start date. Defaults to
  `"1960-01-01"`.

- to:

  Date or character (YYYY-MM-DD). End date. Defaults to today.

- cache:

  Logical. Use cached data if available (default `TRUE`).

## Value

A data frame with columns:

- date:

  Date. Observation date.

- code:

  Character. BoE series code.

- value:

  Numeric. Observation value.

## Details

Series codes can be found via the Bank of England Interactive
Statistical Database at
<https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/boeapps/database/>.

## See also

Other data access:
[`clear_cache()`](https://charlescoverdale.github.io/boe/reference/clear_cache.md)

## Examples

``` r
# \donttest{
op <- options(boe.cache_dir = tempdir())
# Bank Rate since 2000
boe_get("IUDBEDR", from = "2000-01-01")
#> ℹ Using cached data
#> ✔ Using cached data [6ms]
#> 
#> Error in parse_boe_csv(path, series_codes): The Bank of England returned an error.
#> ℹ Check that your series codes are valid: "IUDBEDR"

# Multiple series
boe_get(c("IUDBEDR", "IUDSOIA"), from = "2020-01-01")
#> ℹ Downloading from Bank of England
#> ✔ Downloading from Bank of England [216ms]
```
